# Alan Ruddock

> Associate Professor of Sport Physiology and Performance, Sheffield Hallam University. Co-Founder of Boxing Science. PhD FCASES SFHEA CSci.

## About

Dr Alan Ruddock is an Associate Professor of Sport Physiology and Performance in the School of Sport and Physical Activity at Sheffield Hallam University, UK. He is a Fellow of the Chartered Association of Sport and Exercise Sciences (CASES), a Chartered Scientist (CSci), a Senior Fellow of the Higher Education Academy (SFHEA), an England Athletics qualified Athletics Coach (Level 2) and an ISAK Level 1 Anthropometrist. He co-founded Boxing Science, an applied sport science consultancy supporting elite combat sport athletes including world champions.

## Current Roles

- Associate Professor of Sport Physiology and Performance, Sheffield Hallam University (2023 - present)
- Co-Founder, Boxing Science (2014 - present)
- Director & Chair of Physiology and Nutrition Division, CASES (2024 - present)
- Ethics Lead, School of Sport and Physical Activity, Sheffield Hallam University (2019 - present)
- Course Leader, BSc Sport Technology and BSc Sport and Exercise Science (2021 - 2025)

## Research Impact

- 50+ peer-reviewed publications
- 1,774 citations
- h-index: 26
- i10-index: 31
- ~£178,000 research and consultancy income contributed to, of which ~£52,000 secured as Lead or Principal Investigator
- 4 completed PhDs, 7 current PhD candidates
- 225,000+ reads on ResearchGate
- CASES Applied Practitioner Award recipient (2021)
- Athletics Coach (Level 2, 2023), England Athletics
- ISAK Level 1 Anthropometrist (2026)

## Areas of Expertise

Athletics Coaching, Applied Physiology, Sport Performance, High-Intensity Interval Training (HIIT), Thermoregulation, Hydration, Recovery, Endurance Running, Performance Testing, Strength and Conditioning, Combat Sports Science, Microvascular Function, Velocity-Based Training

## Applied Impact

Led scientific support for boxers in 15 world championship contests, including Olympic Gold medallist and two-time heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua OBE. Delivered workshops to over 500 coaches across the UK, Europe, North America and Asia through Boxing Science, drawing over 300,000 unique visitors a year and over 11 million YouTube views. Provided laboratory testing for Russ Cook ("Hardest Geezer") ahead of his 2024 run across Africa.

## Applied Projects

- Conditioning for world championship boxing (Boxing Science): high-intensity interval responses, load-velocity profiling and weight-making physiology. Scientific support across 15 world championship contests including Anthony Joshua OBE.
- Recovery in elite professional football (Aston Villa FC): recovery interventions evaluated against performance and wellness outcomes in a Premier League environment, via a £40,000 funded doctoral programme embedded in the club.
- Hydration and fluid balance in elite squash (England Squash): fluid and sodium losses were undocumented in squash. Fluid balance, sodium losses and training-day hydration practice measured, published as individualised hydration guidance and a systematic review of the sport's demands.
- Heat acclimation before the 2014 FIFA World Cup (professional soccer match official): 13 sessions over 18 days combining isothermic running and hot water immersion, raising plasma volume 7.1% and high-intensity running performance 29%. Published as a case report in SpringerPlus.
- Operational body armour in specialist police officers (Metropolitan Police Physical Protection Group): authored the foundational 2020 exploratory report applying doctoral thermoregulation research, then oversaw a commissioned study of 147 officers using a novel story stem method.

## Laboratory & Measurement Capability

- Physiological assessment: VO2max and submaximal metabolic testing, gas exchange and RER, lactate profiling, critical power and critical speed, running and cycling economy
- Thermal: core and skin temperature, sweat rate, environmental chamber protocols, heat acclimation
- Neuromuscular: force plates, velocity-based training, isometric and isokinetic strength assessment
- Field: speed and power analysis, blood lactate testing, load-velocity profiling, heart rate variability, wearable validation, remote monitoring in uncontrolled environments
- Governance: Director of CASES (elected Board director); Chair, CASES Physiology and Nutrition Division (2024-2027); School Research Ethics Lead, Sheffield Hallam University, and member of the University Research Ethics Committee; Laboratory Director 2019-2024, securing CASES Laboratory Accreditation in 2024

## Doctoral Supervision

7 current doctoral projects. Embedded with industry partners: Aston Villa FC (recovery methods in elite professional soccer) and Sheffield United FC (speed training in elite professional soccer). Run jointly with international partners: La Trobe University, Melbourne (sleep restriction in team-sport athletes) and Auckland University of Technology, New Zealand (blood flow restriction and recovery). Remaining projects at Sheffield Hallam cover physical training language in tennis, polyphenols and recovery from high-intensity exercise, and anthropometry for fairer disability sport classification. 4 completed doctorates.

## Available For

Industry R&D and product science (physiological testing and study design for sports brands, wearable and technology companies, and product development; independent evaluation of performance claims), athletics coaching (England Athletics qualified, all events, youth to senior), keynote speaking, consultancy, external examining, PhD supervision, advisory boards, and media commentary.

## Education

- MSc in Sport Science, Sheffield Hallam University (2007)
- BSc (Hons.) in Sport Science, Sheffield Hallam University (2005)

## Media & Public Engagement

Expert commentary across broadcast, print and digital platforms including The Times, Wall Street Journal, BBC, Sky Sports, Live Science, Runner's World, and The Conversation.

## Learning Modules

Interactive learning modules at https://alanruddock.com/vo2max/ — short explainers that take one piece of primary research at a time and make it interactive, written for a general audience.

- Module 1: "The number that predicts how long you live" (https://alanruddock.com/vo2max/01-why-vo2max-matters/) — an interactive walk through Myers et al., "Exercise Capacity and Mortality among Men Referred for Exercise Testing", N Engl J Med 2002;346:793-801. Covers what a MET is, how to read a hazard ratio and a confidence interval, what relative risk means and why the reference group matters, and how to read a Kaplan-Meier survival curve. Every figure is rebuilt from the published data.
